Oh man I'm so sorry to hear this. Record conversations. Ask the deep stuff. What does he see in you that reminds him of himself? What would he like his grandchildren to know? What are some lessons he's learned in his life that made him who he is? Favorite holiday memories? Advice on childrearing? Also, something I WISH I would have asked about, and this is a tough one... finances and personal belongings. Now cancer is expensive, and I know I don't fully understand your dad's situation. But when people pass away, an estate (of varying sizes) is born. In a recent experience, I was astounded to see just how quickly loving, caring people can transform into greedy, self absorbed monsters upon feeling entitled to something, anything. They equate money/objects with how much they think that person loved them/how close they were to that person. Even with a clear will, things can go terribly wrong. An aunt who decides she deserves to keep family heirlooms to "complete her set" of what she's inherited. An uncle who decides to keep the life insurance policy that your dad took out decades ago, intending your uncle to distribute it to you if he passed early on (it's difficult to give an insurance policy directly to a minor)... I'm still salty about that one. Just make sure you understand exactly what he owns how he'd like to distribute it, and make sure the rest of the family has an understanding of this as well. The simplest of belongings can be fought over. This is a tough conversation to have, no doubt. But I promise it will save so much grief in the months/years after his passing. Please record it and don't make the same mistake I did.
